note: Every term here is one the examiner reports record candidates confusing or misusing (2022-2025), or one a confused term depends on. The sense is ours, written to match the syllabus wording. Use it exactly, everywhere.

terms.sense: One of the quantities every other is built from: at AS mass, length, time, current, temperature, amount of substance.
terms.homonym_warning: Not a unit: the kilogram is the unit of the base quantity mass.

terms.sense: A unit written as a product or quotient of base units, such as N = kg m s⁻².
An equation whose terms all have the same base units; necessary for it to be correct, not sufficient.
How close a measured value is to the true value.
How close repeated measurements are to each other; also the smallest division a reading is recorded to.
An error that shifts every reading by the same amount or proportion in the same direction, such as a zero error.
terms.homonym_warning: Repeating readings does not reduce it.

terms.sense: Unpredictable scatter of readings about the mean value.
The range either side of a value within which the true value is expected to lie, in the unit of the quantity.
The absolute uncertainty as a percentage of the value itself.
A quantity with magnitude only (mass, energy, work, power, pressure, charge, speed, distance).
A quantity with magnitude and direction (force, displacement, velocity, acceleration, momentum).
The distance moved in a stated direction from the starting point (a vector).
terms.homonym_warning: In waves, the distance of a point from its rest position at an instant.

terms.sense: The rate of change of displacement.
terms.homonym_warning: Not speed, which has no direction.

terms.sense: The rate of change of velocity.
terms.homonym_warning: The gradient of a velocity–time graph, not its height.

terms.sense: The single force with the same effect as all the forces on an object together.
terms.homonym_warning: Not any one of those forces.

terms.sense: The property of an object that resists a change in its motion; measured in kg.
The force of a gravitational field on a mass: W = mg, in newtons.
Mass × velocity; a vector, in N s or kg m s⁻¹.
The constant velocity an object reaches when the resistive force balances the driving force, so the resultant force is zero.
A resistive force from a fluid on a moving object; it acts against the velocity and increases with speed.
The upward force on an object in a fluid, due to the pressure being greater lower down; equal to the weight of fluid displaced.
terms.homonym_warning: Not drag, and not the object’s weight.

terms.sense: A collision in which total kinetic energy is conserved.
terms.homonym_warning: Momentum is conserved in every collision.

terms.sense: The point at which the whole weight of an object can be taken to act.
The turning effect of a force about a point: force × perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action.
Two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide; it turns without any resultant force.
The turning effect of a couple: one of the forces × the perpendicular distance between them.
The state of zero resultant force and zero resultant torque.
terms.homonym_warning: Being at rest is not enough.

terms.sense: Mass per unit volume.
Force per unit area, acting at right angles to the area.
The force multiplied by the distance moved along the line of that force.
Work done, or energy transferred, per unit time.
Useful energy (or power) output ÷ total energy (or power) input.
The increase in length of a stretched object: stretched length minus original length.
The point beyond which force is no longer proportional to extension.
The point beyond which an object will not return to its original shape when the load is removed.
A change of shape that disappears when the load is removed.
A permanent change of shape that stays when the load is removed.
Force per unit cross-sectional area, in Pa.
Extension ÷ original length; it has no unit.
terms.homonym_warning: Not stress, and not strain energy.

terms.sense: Stress ÷ strain, for a material deformed within its limit of proportionality; in Pa.
Force per unit extension, k = F/x, in N m⁻¹.
The energy stored in a deformed object: the area under its force–extension graph.
The maximum displacement of a point on a wave from its rest position.
The distance between two adjacent points on a wave that are in phase, such as neighbouring crests.
The time for one complete oscillation; T = 1/f.
The number of complete oscillations per unit time, in Hz.
How far one oscillation is ahead of another, as a fraction of a cycle, in degrees or radians.
Power per unit area at right angles to the direction the wave travels; proportional to amplitude².
A wave that transfers energy from one place to another.
The pattern formed where two waves of the same frequency travelling in opposite directions superpose; it has nodes and antinodes and transfers no energy along it.
A point on a stationary wave where the amplitude is zero.
A point on a stationary wave where the amplitude is greatest.
Where waves meet, their displacements at each point add to give the resultant displacement there.
The spreading of a wave as it passes through a gap or around an obstacle.
Having a constant phase difference (and so the same frequency).
terms.homonym_warning: Not the same as in phase.

terms.sense: The difference in the distances two waves travel from their sources to a point.
A transverse wave whose oscillations are in one plane only.
The energy converted from electrical to other forms for each coulomb of charge that passes through a component.
Energy transferred from other forms to electrical per unit charge driven round a complete circuit by a source.
The resistance inside a source of e.m.f.; the p.d. across it makes the terminal p.d. less than the e.m.f. when a current flows.
The p.d. across the terminals of a source: e.m.f. minus the p.d. across the internal resistance.
The ratio of the p.d. across a component to the current in it, R = V/I.
terms.homonym_warning: Not the gradient of an I–V graph.

terms.sense: The resistance of a component with a p.d. of one volt across it when the current is one ampere.
The property of a material in R = ρL/A; in Ω m.
The number of charge carriers per unit volume, n in I = Anvq.
The number of protons plus neutrons in a nucleus (A).
The number of protons in a nucleus (Z).
Nuclei of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
A particle with the same mass as its partner and the opposite charge.
A particle with no smaller constituents: quarks and leptons.
terms.homonym_warning: Protons and neutrons are not fundamental.

terms.sense: A particle made of quarks: a baryon or a meson.
A hadron made of three quarks, such as the proton and the neutron.
A hadron made of one quark and one antiquark.
A fundamental particle not made of quarks, such as the electron and the neutrino.
The readings as taken, before any calculation.
An axis that does not start at zero.
terms.homonym_warning: The y-intercept cannot be read off where the x-axis does not start at zero.

terms.sense: A single straight line or smooth curve with points balanced either side of it.
